verdict.rationale: The IRS documents two machine-to-machine filing channels: IRIS Application to Application (A2A) intake for information returns, and MeF XML system-to-system transmission. These suggest programmatic submission of many returns, but both are gated behind credentialing (a Transmitter Control Code, or authorized e-file provider status with up to 45-day approval and fingerprinting). The EIN assistant explicitly allows only 1 EIN per responsible party per day, so not every service supports bulk work. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of batch/bulk submission semantics (multiple items per transmission), bulk operations beyond information returns and e-file, open access without provider enrollment, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: IRIS "receives information through two intake channels: IRIS Taxpayer Portal/UI and IRIS Application to Application (A2A)"
MeF uses the widely accepted Extensible Markup Language (XML) format.
